transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what really scared me enough to come in today is that I’ve been hearing my name called out. It usually comes from the hallway at home, but it even happened once at the warehouse where I work, when I knew nobody else was around. It's just... it sounds as clear and real as my husband standing right next to me. But when I look, nobody is there.
How long have you been hearing this voice calling your name—days, weeks, or longer?

Well, it's been about three weeks. The whole thing, really. Like, going from being all wound up and restless, to starting to hear my name, and then just crashing... yeah, that whole change has been going on for about three weeks now.
In the past few weeks, have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications/supplements?
No, I haven't. I don't really drink, and I definitely don't use any drugs. And I haven't started taking any new medications or, you know, supplements or anything like that either.
During that period when you felt really wound up and restless, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt full of energy?

Yeah, exactly. For a while there, I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But the weird thing was, I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up just completely ready to go. It honestly felt like sleeping was just a waste of time, you know? Like it was getting in the way of all the projects I needed to get done.

When you hear your name being called, does that tend to happen more during the times you're feeling wound up and full of energy, or during the times you're feeling low and crashed, or does it happen regardless of how your mood is at that moment?

It happened mostly when I was feeling really wound up. You know, during that time when I was barely sleeping and just talking constantly, feeling like I had to fix everything around the house. That's when I heard it. Before all that started, and then after I crashed and got really low and withdrawn... I haven't heard the voice during those times. It was just during that really high-energy stretch.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a distinct manic episode (approximately 3 weeks) characterized by decreased need for sleep with high energy, psychomotor agitation, pressured activity, and grandiosity-driven behavior (compulsion to 'fix everything'), followed by a depressive crash—consistent with a bipolar course. During the manic phase, she experienced mood-congruent auditory hallucinations (hearing her name called) that occurred exclusively during the high-energy period and resolved as mood shifted, indicating psychotic features occurring only within the mood episode rather than an independent psychotic disorder. Substance use, medication changes, and other medical causes were ruled out. This pattern—manic episode with psychotic features embedded temporally within the mood disturbance—supports Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic, severe with psychotic features (F31.2), rather than schizoaffective disorder (psychosis present only during mood episode, not persisting independently) or unipolar psychotic depression (clear antecedent manic symptoms present).
